requirements.heading: Structure of This Document
requirements.text: Any examples in this section MUST NOT be taken as specification of the formal syntax of any part of a message.

requirements.heading: Structure of This Document
requirements.text: The syntax included in section 3 represents messages as they MUST be created.

requirements.heading: Structure of This Document
requirements.text: There are also notes in section 3 to indicate if any of the options specified in the syntax SHOULD be used over any of the others.

requirements.heading: Structure of This Document
requirements.text: As such, these elements MUST be interpreted by parsers of messages in order to be conformant to this specification.

requirements.heading: Structure of This Document
requirements.text: However, since items in this syntax have been determined to be non-interoperable or to cause significant problems for recipients of messages, they MUST NOT be generated by creators of conformant messages.

requirements.heading: Line Length Limits
requirements.text: Each line of characters MUST be no more than 998 characters, and SHOULD be no more than 78 characters, excluding the CRLF.

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: A field name MUST be composed of printable US-ASCII characters (i.e., characters that have values between 33 and 126, inclusive), except colon.

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: A field body MUST NOT include CR and LF except when used in "folding" and "unfolding", as described in section 2.2.3.

requirements.heading: Header Fields
requirements.text: All field bodies MUST conform to the syntax described in sections 3 and 4 of this specification.

requirements.heading: Long Header Fields
requirements.text: Note: Though structured field bodies are defined in such a way that folding can take place between many of the lexical tokens (and even within some of the lexical tokens), folding SHOULD be limited to placing the CRLF at higher-level syntactic breaks.

requirements.heading: Body
requirements.text: o CR and LF MUST only occur together as CRLF; they MUST NOT appear independently in the body.

requirements.heading: Body
requirements.text: o Lines of characters in the body MUST be limited to 998 characters, and SHOULD be limited to 78 characters, excluding the CRLF.

requirements.heading: Introduction
requirements.text: Messages that are conformant to this specification MUST conform to the syntax in this section.

requirements.heading: Introduction
requirements.text: If there are options in this section where one option SHOULD be generated, that is indicated either in the prose or in a comment next to the syntax.

requirements.heading: Introduction
requirements.text: In all cases, these productions are to be ignored for the purposes of generating legal Internet messages and MUST NOT be used as part of such a message.

requirements.heading: Introduction
requirements.text: However, when interpreting messages, these tokens MUST be honored as part of the legal syntax.

requirements.heading: Folding White Space and Comments
requirements.text: However, where CFWS occurs in this specification, it MUST NOT be inserted in such a way that any line of a folded header field is made up entirely of WSP characters and nothing else.

requirements.heading: Date and Time Specification
requirements.text: Though folding white space is permitted throughout the date-time specification, it is RECOMMENDED that a single space be used in each place that FWS appears (whether it is required or optional); some older implementations will not interpret longer sequences of folding white space correctly.

requirements.heading: Date and Time Specification
requirements.text: The date and time-of-day SHOULD express local time.

requirements.heading: Date and Time Specification
requirements.text: The form "+0000" SHOULD be used to indicate a time zone at Universal Time.

requirements.heading: Date and Time Specification
requirements.text: A date-time specification MUST be semantically valid.

requirements.heading: Date and Time Specification
requirements.text: That is, the day-of-week (if included) MUST be the day implied by the date, the numeric day-of-month MUST be between 1 and the number of days allowed for the specified month (in the specified year), the time-of-day MUST be in the range 00:00:00 through 23:59:60 (the number of seconds allowing for a leap second; see [RFC1305]), and the last two digits of the zone MUST be within the range 00 through 59.

requirements.heading: Address Specification
requirements.text: Since the meaning of the information in a comment is unspecified, implementations SHOULD use the full name-addr form of the mailbox, instead of the legacy form, to specify the display name associated with a mailbox.

requirements.heading: Address Specification
requirements.text: Also, because some legacy implementations interpret the comment, comments generally SHOULD NOT be used in address fields to avoid confusing such implementations.

requirements.heading: Addr-Spec Specification
requirements.text: If the string can be represented as a dot-atom (that is, it contains no characters other than atext characters or "." surrounded by atext characters), then the dot-atom form SHOULD be used and the quoted- string form SHOULD NOT be used.

requirements.heading: Addr-Spec Specification
requirements.text: Comments and folding white space SHOULD NOT be used around the "@" in the addr-spec.

requirements.heading: Overall Message Syntax
requirements.text: Lines in a message MUST be a maximum of 998 characters excluding the CRLF, but it is RECOMMENDED that lines be limited to 78 characters excluding the CRLF.

requirements.heading: Overall Message Syntax
requirements.text: (See section 2.1.1 for explanation.) In a message body, though all of the characters listed in the text rule MAY be used, the use of US-ASCII control characters (values 1 through 8, 11, 12, and 14 through 31) is discouraged since their interpretation by receivers for display is not guaranteed.

requirements.heading: Field Definitions
requirements.text: However, for the purposes of this specification, header fields SHOULD NOT be reordered when a message is transported or transformed.

requirements.heading: Field Definitions
requirements.text: More importantly, the trace header fields and resent header fields MUST NOT be reordered, and SHOULD be kept in blocks prepended to the message.

requirements.heading: Originator Fields
requirements.text: If the from field contains more than one mailbox specification in the mailbox- list, then the sender field, containing the field name "Sender" and a single mailbox specification, MUST appear in the message.

requirements.heading: Originator Fields
requirements.text: In either case, an optional reply-to field MAY also be included, which contains the field name "Reply-To" and a comma-separated list of one or more addresses.

requirements.heading: Originator Fields
requirements.text: by a single mailbox and the author and transmitter are identical, the "Sender:" field SHOULD NOT be used.

requirements.heading: Originator Fields
requirements.text: Otherwise, both fields SHOULD appear.

requirements.heading: Originator Fields
requirements.text: In the absence of the "Reply-To:" field, replies SHOULD by default be sent to the mailbox(es) specified in the "From:" field unless otherwise specified by the person composing the reply.

requirements.heading: Originator Fields
requirements.text: In all cases, the "From:" field SHOULD NOT contain any mailbox that does not belong to the author(s) of the message.

requirements.heading: Destination Address Fields
requirements.text: When a message is a reply to another message, the mailboxes of the authors of the original message (the mailboxes in the "From:" field) or mailboxes specified in the "Reply-To:" field (if it exists) MAY appear in the "To:" field of the reply since these would normally be the primary recipients of the reply.

requirements.heading: Destination Address Fields
requirements.text: When such a reply is formed, addresses in the "To:" and "Cc:" fields of the original message MAY appear in the "Cc:" field of the reply, since these are normally secondary recipients of the reply.

requirements.heading: Destination Address Fields
requirements.text: If a "Bcc:" field is present in the original message, addresses in that field MAY appear in the "Bcc:" field of the reply, but they SHOULD NOT appear in the "To:" or "Cc:" fields.

requirements.heading: Identification Fields
requirements.text: Though listed as optional in the table in section 3.6, every message SHOULD have a "Message-ID:" field.

requirements.heading: Identification Fields
requirements.text: Furthermore, reply messages SHOULD have "In-Reply-To:" and "References:" fields as appropriate and as described below.

requirements.heading: Identification Fields
requirements.text: However, later in this section, the use of a domain for the right-hand side of the "@" is RECOMMENDED.

requirements.heading: Identification Fields
requirements.text: The message identifier (msg-id) itself MUST be a globally unique identifier for a message.

requirements.heading: Identification Fields
requirements.text: The generator of the message identifier MUST guarantee that the msg-id is unique.

requirements.heading: Identification Fields
requirements.text: Though other algorithms will work, it is RECOMMENDED that the right-hand side contain some domain identifier (either of the host itself or otherwise) such that the generator of the message identifier can guarantee the uniqueness of the left-hand side within the scope of that domain.

requirements.heading: Informational Fields
requirements.text: When used in a reply, the field body MAY start with the string "Re: " (an abbreviation of the Latin "in re", meaning "in the matter of") followed by the contents of the "Subject:" field body of the original message.

requirements.heading: Resent Fields
requirements.text: Resent fields SHOULD be added to any message that is reintroduced by a user into the transport system.

requirements.heading: Resent Fields
requirements.text: A separate set of resent fields SHOULD be added each time this is done.

requirements.heading: Resent Fields
requirements.text: All of the resent fields corresponding to a particular resending of the message SHOULD be grouped together.

requirements.heading: Resent Fields
requirements.text: When resent fields are used, the "Resent-From:" and "Resent-Date:" fields MUST be sent.

requirements.heading: Resent Fields
requirements.text: The "Resent-Message-ID:" field SHOULD be sent.

requirements.heading: Resent Fields
requirements.text: "Resent-Sender:" SHOULD NOT be used if "Resent-Sender:" would be identical to "Resent-From:".

requirements.heading: Resent Fields
requirements.text: They MUST NOT be used in the normal processing of replies or other such automatic actions on messages.

requirements.heading: Resent Fields
requirements.text: The resent fields are only informational and MUST NOT be used in the normal processing of replies.

requirements.heading: Optional Fields
requirements.text: They MUST conform to the syntax of an optional-field.

requirements.heading: Optional Fields
requirements.text: The field names of any optional field MUST NOT be identical to any field name specified elsewhere in this document.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Syntax
requirements.text: Though these syntactic forms MUST NOT be generated according to the grammar in section 3, they MUST be accepted and parsed by a conformant receiver.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Syntax
requirements.text: Note: This section identifies syntactic forms that any implementation MUST reasonably interpret.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Folding White Space
requirements.text: In the obsolete syntax, any amount of folding white space MAY be inserted where the obs-FWS rule is allowed.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Date and Time
requirements.text: However, because of the error in [RFC0822], they SHOULD all be considered equivalent to "-0000" unless there is out-of-band information confirming their meaning.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Date and Time
requirements.text: Any such time zone whose meaning is not known SHOULD be considered equivalent to "-0000" unless there is out-of-band information confirming their meaning.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Addressing
requirements.text: When interpreting addresses, the route portion SHOULD be ignored.

requirements.heading: Obsolete Destination Address Fields
requirements.text: When multiple occurrences of destination address fields occur in a message, they SHOULD be treated as if the address list in the first occurrence of the field is combined with the address lists of the subsequent occurrences by adding a comma and concatenating.
